title: Accepting back, repackaging and re-dispensing a multi-drug-single-dose package to the same patient
subtopic: Return and repackaging of multi-drug-single-dose packaging
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.08(4)(a), a pharmacy or pharmacist may accept a return of a multi-drug-single-dose package that the pharmacy previously dispensed for the purpose of repackaging and re-dispensing to that same patient. If the patient's medication was discontinued, a pharmacy may remove the discontinued drug(s) and re-dispense the remaining medications in the multi-drug-single-dose package to the same patient; if the patient's drug therapy changed, a pharmacy may remove the discontinued drug(s), may add new medication(s), and re-dispense the package to the same patient. A pharmacy shall label the package in accordance with 247 CMR 9.08(5) prior to re-dispensing, and shall implement policies and procedures pertaining to security and accountability of controlled substances during return and repackaging. Under 9.08(4)(b), a licensee may not return any medication removed from a multi-drug-single-dose package to inventory, and may not dispense any medication removed from such a package to any patient other than the patient who returned it. Under 9.08(4)(c), a pharmacy shall maintain a record that accounts for and documents any repackaging, removal, or re-dispensing of any medication it previously dispensed in a multi-drug-single-dose package, and the record shall identify the pharmacist making the change.
exam_relevance: Tests the same-pharmacy, same-patient limits on taking back a multi-drug-single-dose package, the ban on returning removed medication to inventory or giving it to another patient, relabeling before re-dispensing, and the record naming the pharmacist who made the change.

authority.name: Compliance Packaging: Return and Repackaging of Multi-drug-single-dose Packaging

common_confusions: Returning a discontinued drug removed from a multi-drug-single-dose package to stock.
Accepting a multi-drug-single-dose package that another pharmacy dispensed.
Keeping a repackaging record that does not identify the pharmacist who made the change.
